title: Incubator World Phylogeny Record (v0)
description: One record per WORLD in the Incubator research tree. The Incubator develops by failure-driven forking: World N+1 exists ONLY because World N exposed a specific, characterized ceiling. This file is therefore the experimental history of the Incubator itself, and it is the artifact that distinguishes a research program from a sequence of demos. FAILED WORLDS ARE NEVER OVERWRITTEN OR DELETED -- they are fossils, and a world that cleanly exposes a ceiling is often more scientifically useful than one that looks successful.

parent_world_id.description: null only for World-0, the root

sibling_arm.description: when several worlds fork from one ceiling as competing interventions, the arm label (e.g. duplication / protected-module / control). Siblings share a parent AND a preregistered prediction set.

engine_source_hash.description: build-derived identity of the engine that ran this world

world_physics_hash.description: identity of instruction set + generator distribution + cost table. MUST be inside the release identity, never a mutable runtime file.

checkpoint_id.description: the parent checkpoint this world was forked from, if the fork was a state fork rather than a fresh physics

intent.description: WHY this world exists. A world with no antecedent ceiling is not a scientific fork -- it is a new program, and must be labelled as such.

antecedent_ceiling.description: the characterized limiting regime observed in the parent (e.g. an F-class from the OEE Failure Atlas) that motivated this fork

ceiling_evidence.description: what measurement established that ceiling in the parent, including the null it beat

proposed_mechanism.description: the causal mechanism hypothesised to produce the ceiling

intervention.description: exactly what changed in the physics/operators/economy relative to the parent. MUST be a single named change per arm where possible.

is_control.description: true if this arm changes nothing causal and exists to isolate the intervention

is_new_program.description: true if this world does NOT descend from a measured ceiling. Such worlds are permitted but must be labelled, because they are exploratory rather than confirmatory.

preregistration.description: Sealed BEFORE the world runs, via the engine's irreversible experiment-commit boundary. A fork whose prediction was written after its result is not evidence.

prediction.description: what the intervention is predicted to do to the REGIME, not merely to performance

decision_rule.description: the single pre-committed test and threshold

sealed_commit_seq.description: ledger event_seq of the sealing commit; null means NOT SEALED and the result is exploratory only

observed.description: What the world actually did. Populated after the run; never edited afterwards -- corrections are appended as errata.

regime_classification.description: the dominant dynamical regime observed, drawn from the OEE Failure Atlas class set (refined taxonomy), or NOVEL_REGIME if none fits

e_level_reached.description: highest level of the Prometheus OEE hierarchy for which COUNTERFACTUAL evidence exists. Behavioural impression is never sufficient. Regression is permitted and expected.

e_level_evidence.description: the ablation or transplant that established it

failure_landscape_change.description: how the failure topology differed from the parent, measured under rarefaction on capability-DISJOINT coordinates

ceiling_observed.description: the limiting regime this world itself exposed -- i.e. the antecedent_ceiling for its children

conventional_metrics.description: fitness, success rate, efficiency, diversity -- recorded so we can test whether failure geometry added anything the cheap metrics did not

scale_actually_run.description: Recorded so that 'it did not compound' can be separated from 'we could not afford to let it compound'.

independent_runs.description: the replicate count for population-level claims. A single run is n=1 and supports no population claim.

killed_by.description: which preregistered kill criterion fired, if any

status.description: ABANDONED worlds are RETAINED, never deleted. Reason must be recorded in notes.

next_forks.description: Children this world motivates. Populating this is how the research tree grows: a ceiling with no proposed fork is an unfinished result.

scale_is_the_intervention.description: true if the ONLY change is more time/population/compute. Such forks are permitted but must be declared, because 'run it longer' must be an explicit hypothesis rather than the reflex response to every plateau.

reconstruction.description: Everything needed to re-run this world exactly. A world that cannot be reconstructed is not evidence.

analysis_code_hash.description: the analysis is part of the instrument; a silently changed analysis invalidates cross-world comparison

$comment: DESIGN RULES a future maintainer must not 'improve' away: (1) A world exists because a MEASURED ceiling motivated it -- worlds added for elegance or biological realism must be flagged is_new_program=true. (2) The prediction is sealed BEFORE the run or the result is exploratory. (3) Failed and abandoned worlds are retained permanently. (4) 'Run it longer / bigger' is a declarable intervention, never a default. (5) e_level_reached requires counterfactual evidence, never a suggestive trajectory. (6) This file records the falsification ladder WE climb; it must never become a curriculum the ORGANISMS climb -- that distinction is the foundation of the whole program.
